title: Public booking attaches a reservation to any existing guest profile matched by email; lookup then discloses that guest's loyalty number, points and QR text, and online check-in overwrites the guest's ID data
lower_trust_principal: Anonymous internet user who knows a guest's email address and last name
boundary_crossed: Unauthenticated public booking API -> another guest's profile (Guests.guest row, loyalty membership) in the group

entrypoint.description: book(): Guest::where('email', $data['guest']['email'])->first() reuses an existing guest row with no proof that the caller owns that email; member_number on line 118 likewise binds the booking to Membership->guest without the last-name check used elsewhere

sink.description: lookup(): returns loyalty number, tier, points_balance and 'OPES-LOYALTY:<number>' QR text for the guest attached to the booking (and guest first/last name on line 162)

propagation.description: reservation created with guest_id of the victim's profile
lookup proof is confirmation/public_code + guest last name (strcasecmp) -> attacker knows both since they created the booking under the victim's profile
manage token is issued for that reservation, unlocking ManageController::checkin
digital check-in writes id_number, birth_date, address etc. onto the victim's Guest row ($guest->update(array_filter([...])))

intended_control: Guest identity on the public site is proven by confirmation number + last name; loyalty data should only be returned to the member
observed_or_expected_result: Attacker POSTs /api/v1/booking/{group}/reservations with guest.email = victim email and guest.last_name = victim last name (first name arbitrary), receives confirmation + manage token; POST reservations/lookup with that confirmation + victim last name returns the victim's loyalty card number, tier and points balance plus the QR string staff scan for earn/redeem; the attacker can also submit online check-in that rewrites the victim's stored ID number / birth date / address, and the fake booking appears under the victim's profile (member portal, history, marketing consent flag on the shared profile is untouched but the reservation and any special_requests are theirs). Cancellation later is free when the plan is refundable.
conditions: Victim has a Guest row (any prior stay) in the group; loyalty disclosure additionally requires an active membership
Attacker knows victim email + last name (both commonly public)
smallest_fix: In book(): never attach a public booking to an existing guest by email alone; create a new guest row (or only reuse when the member_number + last name pair matches, as member() does on line 228-236) and require last-name match for member_number on line 118. In lookup(): drop the 'loyalty' block (or only return it when the request also carries the member's own credential).
regression_test_idea: Feature test: seed guest G (email e, membership M); POST public book with guest.email=e, last_name=G.last_name from an anonymous client; assert reservation.guest_id != G.id and lookup response has no 'loyalty' key.

title: Public booking honours staff-chosen corporate codes (e.g. 'ACME') and books on the company's contract: negotiated rates, allotment rooms and company_id on the reservation, with a 300/min validity oracle
boundary_crossed: Public booking API -> B2B corporate contract (confidential negotiated rate, allotment, company account)

entrypoint.description: book()/availability() accept corporate_code (max 24 chars) from anyone

sink.description: bookingFields(): reservation gets company_id, contract rate_plan_id, room_block_id (allotment) and source corporate:<code>

propagation.description: find(): CorporateContract::where('code', strtoupper(trim($code)))->where('active', true) -- code is the only secret
codes are staff-chosen, regex [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,20}, typically company names
availability() (throttle public-read 300/min) decorates offers with the contract when the code is valid -> code-guessing oracle

intended_control: Corporate contract bookings are restricted to the company's travellers
observed_or_expected_result: Guessing a short code lets anyone consume a company's allotment and book at the confidential negotiated rate with company_id set (depending on folio routing, charges may route to the company's city ledger).
conditions: Corporate contracts with guessable codes exist (default usage)
Impact on billing depends on folio routing rules for company_id reservations (not verified here)
smallest_fix: Require a second factor for corporate bookings on the public site (email domain of the company, or per-company random booking token of >= 64 bits generated by the system instead of a staff-chosen code); throttle corporate_code lookups per IP with a lockout; never set company_id as bill-to from a public booking without staff confirmation.
regression_test_idea: Test that availability with a wrong corporate_code returns the same body as without one, and that a public booking with a valid code yields a reservation with company_id null / status pending staff validation.

title: CSV/XLSX exports write guest- and public-supplied text (names, special requests, cover notes, review comments) unescaped: cells starting with = + - @ become formulas in Excel
lower_trust_principal: Anonymous public user (booking form, careers application, review, demo request)
boundary_crossed: Public form input -> staff workstation via downloaded export

entrypoint.description: guest.first_name / last_name / special_requests accepted as free strings (max 100/1000)

sink.description: csv(): fputcsv($out, $r, ';', '"', '') with cell() (line 64) passing strings through unchanged; same in app/Modules/Accounting/Support/Sheets.php line 41 and the xlsx writers

intended_control: Exports are trusted spreadsheets for staff
observed_or_expected_result: A guest named '=HYPERLINK("http://evil","click")' or '=cmd|/C calc!A0' (with DDE prompts) lands in a report export; Excel evaluates it on the staff machine.
conditions: Staff opens the export in Excel/LibreOffice with formulas enabled (default for CSV)
smallest_fix: In Exporter::cell() and Sheets::csv(): if a string starts with one of = + - @ \t \r, prefix it with a single quote (') or a space; for xlsx force string cell type.
regression_test_idea: Unit test Exporter::csv with a row ['=1+1'] asserting the output cell starts with "'=".

title: Outside APP_ENV=production, providers without credentials fall back to DryRunGateway whose status() auto-succeeds: the public status poll settles a deposit/pay-link as paid with no money
lower_trust_principal: Anonymous payer on the booking site or a pay link
boundary_crossed: Public status poll -> folio payment posting / reservation deposit_paid

entrypoint.description: status(): public GET with manage token calls PaymentService::refresh()

sink.description: refresh(): $status from DryRunGateway::status() (Drivers/DryRunGateway.php line 158-162 returns 'succeeded') -> settle() posts the folio payment and increments deposit_paid

propagation.description: driverFor(): DryRunGateway whenever the hotel has no credentials and app()->isProduction() is false

intended_control: Dry run is for development only; production refuses unconfigured providers
observed_or_expected_result: Any staging/demo/UAT deployment (APP_ENV=staging, demo, local) lets guests mark bookings as paid; a production host misconfigured with APP_ENV != production is fully exposed.
conditions: APP_ENV is not 'production' on an internet-facing instance (e.g. the demo/landing environment that ships DemoLoginController accounts)
smallest_fix: Gate DryRunGateway on an explicit config flag (payments.dry_run=true) that defaults to false, independent of APP_ENV, and log loudly when enabled; refuse dry-run intents on the public channel.
regression_test_idea: Test with APP_ENV=staging and no gateway credentials: public deposit + status must return 'gateway-not-configured' (422) rather than a succeeded intent.

title: Public digital check-in stores the ID photo from a base64 data URL with only a prefix check (no magic-byte/finfo validation), unlike the staff path
lower_trust_principal: Guest with a manage token (or attacker holding one via the email-reuse issue)
boundary_crossed: Public form -> private local disk file later served inline to staff

sink.description: storePhoto(): Storage::disk('local')->put("checkins/{hotel}/{id}-id.<ext>", base64 bytes) with extension taken from the declared mime, bytes never checked

propagation.description: staff path uses finfo buffer check (store()) and Storage::disk('local')->response() serves by extension-derived mime; nosniff is set by SecurityHeaders so browser execution is unlikely

intended_control: Only JPEG/PNG/WebP images accepted (as enforced on the staff path)
observed_or_expected_result: Arbitrary bytes up to 2 MB written under storage/app/checkins with a .jpg/.png/.webp name; when later decoded by image libraries (thumbnails, PDF embedding) malformed input reaches the decoder. No direct code execution path identified.
conditions: Staff or a PDF renderer later opens the file
smallest_fix: Reuse the finfo-based store() logic from FrontDeskExtrasController (check magic bytes/mime of the decoded bytes before writing).

title: Guest room-service order idempotency key (client_uuid) is looked up hotel-wide, not per reservation: another guest's order is returned for a colliding/guessed uuid
lower_trust_principal: Guest holding a signed ordering link for their own reservation
boundary_crossed: Own reservation -> other reservation's GuestOrder (id, total, status, pos check id)

entrypoint.description: place(): client_uuid is any string <= 64 chars

sink.description: GuestOrder::where('client_uuid', $clientUuid)->first() without reservation_id filter; the order is returned as if it were the caller's

intended_control: Retry protection for one guest's own double tap
observed_or_expected_result: If uuids are predictable on the client, a guest can read another in-house guest's order totals/check ids and skip placing their own order; also an attacker can poison a uuid so that the real guest's first order silently returns the attacker's record.
smallest_fix: Add ->where('reservation_id', $r->id) to the client_uuid lookup (and a unique index on (reservation_id, client_uuid)).
regression_test_idea: Two reservations, same client_uuid: second place() must create a new order.

title: Channel inbound webhooks for connections in 'sandbox' environment without a webhook_secret accept unsigned bookings
lower_trust_principal: Anyone who learns a sandbox connection uuid
boundary_crossed: Unauthenticated POST -> reservation import into the hotel

sink.description: verify(): return $c->environment === 'sandbox' when webhook_secret is empty -> true

intended_control: Each connection authenticates its provider by HMAC
observed_or_expected_result: Fake OTA bookings (and XML payloads up to the body limit) can be injected into a hotel whose connection was left in sandbox with no secret; the uuid (whereUuid) is the only secret and appears in provider configuration screens/logs.
conditions: A connection with environment=sandbox, receive_reservations=true and no webhook_secret is reachable on the public host
smallest_fix: Require a webhook_secret for every connection that receives reservations, sandbox included (generate one at connection creation).
regression_test_idea: Sandbox connection without secret: unsigned POST must be 401.

title: Edge sync signature has a 300 s clock-skew window but no nonce; pull requests (and any non-idempotent future endpoint) can be replayed within the window
lower_trust_principal: Network attacker who captures one edge request (TLS termination / proxy logs)
boundary_crossed: Captured request -> cloud edge API as that node

entrypoint.description: authenticate(): only timestamp skew and HMAC(method, path, ts, body-hash) are checked

sink.description: pull(): moves pull_cursor backwards/forwards to the replayed cursor and returns the hotel's change feed again

propagation.description: push is idempotent via edge_batches batch_key so push replay is harmless

observed_or_expected_result: Replayed pull re-discloses the feed to whoever captured the request and resets the node's pull cursor; limited because TLS normally protects the channel.
conditions: Attacker can observe traffic between edge and cloud
smallest_fix: Include a random nonce header in the signature and reject (node, nonce) seen within the skew window (cache), or sign over the cursor and require strictly increasing timestamps per node.
regression_test_idea: Replay the same signed pull twice: second must be 401.

title: PublicBookingResolver answers 403 'Invalid link' for a wrong manage token but 404 for an unknown reference, and 422 'ambiguous' when several bookings share a confirmation number: existence oracle on booking references
boundary_crossed: Public API -> existence of a reservation reference / confirmation number in a group

entrypoint.description: fail(404) when empty vs fail(403) on token mismatch (line 110) vs fail(422) ambiguous (line 121)

sink.description: 422 'Several bookings share this confirmation number' returned before any ownership proof when lastName/token are absent (review path allows token null + last_name)

intended_control: Comment: 'Never picks the first of several matches' and uniform 404 on name mismatch
observed_or_expected_result: Distinguishable responses let an attacker confirm that a confirmation number / 8-char public_code exists (public_code space is 31^8 so brute force is impractical; sequential confirmation numbers are trivially enumerable but reveal only existence).
conditions: public-write throttle 20/min per ip+uri limits volume
smallest_fix: Return the same 404 body for not-found, bad token and name mismatch; only emit the 'ambiguous' hint after the last name or token matched at least one candidate (it already does for the name path; make the token path identical).
regression_test_idea: Assert identical status/body for unknown reference and wrong token.

title: Booking-site deposit and pay flows forward an arbitrary return_url to Orange Money / card gateway as return_url and cancel_url (open redirect after payment)
lower_trust_principal: Attacker crafting a deposit request on behalf of a guest (requires manage token) or any pay-link payer
boundary_crossed: Public input -> third-party payment page redirect target

sink.description: return_url / cancel_url sent to the provider; CardGateway.php line 40 likewise

intended_control: Return to the booking site after payment
observed_or_expected_result: After paying, the guest is sent by the provider to an attacker-chosen site (phishing continuation); needs the attacker to initiate the intent whose redirect_url the victim then follows.
conditions: Attacker must get the victim to use an intent they created (e.g. shared link with the provider redirect_url)
smallest_fix: Validate return_url host against config('app.url') (or allow only paths) before storing it.
